To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

gene transfer with a novel E1/E3/ E4-deleted adenovi-rus vector induces persistent expression of the human apo A-I transgene and that transgene DNA turnover is dissociated from hepatotoxicity and is independent of a cell-mediated adaptive immune response against viral proteins.

gene transfer with a gutted vector containing the hα1-antitripsin.gA-I.apo E enhancer expression cassette induces persistent transgene expression in the absence of toxicity and that transgene DNA turnover is E4 ORF3 and E4ORF4 dependent but independent of hepatotoxicity and an adaptive cellular immune reaction.

gene transfer with an helper-virus independent, E1/E3-deleted vector containing a transgene under the control of the human α1-AT promoter and the human apo E-enhancer induces persistent expression of this transgene without hepatotoxicity and that the expression cassette determines transgene persistence.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of adenoviral vectors for gene transfer into the mouse liver.
the development of gene transfer vectors for gene therapy and gene expression studies.
the use of adenoviral vectors in gene therapy and the development of novel adenoviral vectors for the treatment of atherosclerosis and cancer.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the hAAT.4xapo E expression cassette is an efficient and safe promoter/enhancer combination for persistent transgene expression in the liver after transfer with a gutted adenovirus.
the E1/E4-deleted viral backbone is the key determinant of the transgene DNA persistence.
the E4 gene products are responsible for transgene DNA destabilization, but not for hepatotoxicity.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the hAAT.4xapoEnh expression cassette is a good candidate to be used in E1/E3 deleted adenoviral vectors for persistent expression in the liver.

we have developed a gene transfer strategy for persistent expression of human apolipoprotein A-I in the liver of C57BL/ 6 mice that is associated with stable transgene DNA and absence of hepatocytotoxicity.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the expression cassette and the presence of the E4 ORF’s are important for the stability of transgene DNA in the absence of helper viruses.
the E4 gene products of adenovirus are involved in transgene DNA turnover in trans, but not in transgene DNA persistence.
the use of E4-deleted vectors may be a way to avoid the use of helper-viruses in the production of adenoviral vectors for gene therapy.
